This is a yoga breathing method called 4–7–8 breathing method. After 2–3 months of practice, you will see significant changes in your physiology, your heart rate and blood pressure will decrease, and your digestive function will improve.
Breathe in a long breath for 8 seconds, strong enough to blow your lips.
Inhale through your nose for 4 seconds each time. Then hold your breath for 7 seconds. The watch will vibrate when inhaling.
Do not breathe excessively, and pay attention to slow breathing when practicing.
Be careful not to focus too much on time while breathing, this will make you awake.
People who are weak, please do not hold their breath for too long, which may cause dizziness.Please do according to your physical condition.
Users with high blood pressure and cardiovascular diseases are not suitable for this method

1.Turn off your phone’s Bluetooth, wait a moment, and then turn it back on.

How to measure blood oxygen saturation?
1. Wear the device normally and keep it still.
2. Open the blood oxygen function on the device side and click Measurement (refer to the actual page).
3. During the measurement, keep your body still and wait for the measurement value with the screen facing up.

To ensure the accuracy of blood oxygen measurement, please avoid the wrist joint and fit the device to the skin, and adjust the tightness to wear it normally. Select blood oxygen in the device menu, tap the screen to measure blood oxygen, and stay relaxed during the measurement and wait for the measurement results to come out.

Oxygen saturation is the percentage of oxygen–bound oxyhemoglobin in the blood that accounts for the total amount of hemoglobin that can be combined, that is, the concentration of blood oxygen in the blood, which is an important physiological parameter of the respiratory cycle.
normal blood pressure: \n 90MMHG < systolic blood pressure < 140MMHG \n 60MMHG < diastolic blood pressure < 90MMHG

Before starting exercise, it is necessary to assess your physical condition. This includes measuring basic physical indicators such as height, weight, body fat percentage, blood pressure, and heart rate. At the same time, you should also consider whether you have any underlying conditions (such as heart disease, arthritis, etc.) or old injuries. If so, it is recommended to consult a doctor\'s opinion first to ensure that exercise training will not harm your body.
How to start a workout training?

Such as fast walking, jogging, cycling, aerobics, etc., this kind of exercise can improve cardiorespiratory function, calorie consumption, suitable for most people, the speed control at about 100 – 120 steps per minute, each time lasts about 30 minutes.

This includes machine training (e.g. dumbbells, barbells) and self–weight training (e.g. squats, planks). For beginners, start with simple self–weight training such as 2 – 3 sets of 10 – 15 reps of squats and push–ups per day.
Exercises such as yoga and Pilates are effective in improving flexibility and balance. Flexibility training sessions can be scheduled 2 – 3 times a week for 30 – 60 minutes each time.
Warming up is an essential part of athletic training. It helps the body get into motion faster, increases muscle temperature and flexibility, and reduces the risk of injury.
Stretching after exercise helps to relax muscles, reduce muscle soreness and improve flexibility.

Heart strength is a comprehensive indicator of heart health. The score is determined by the heart rate, HRV index and abnormal ECG status in a calm state. The higher the score, the stronger the comprehensive function of the heart.

Heart rate variability is an important indicator to determine the ability of autonomic nervous system to regulate the cardiovascular system. The higher the heart rate variability, the better the ability of the surface autonomic nerve to regulate the cardiovascular system, and the healthier the cardiovascular system.

Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measures the difference in time between heartbeats. HRV is calculated from the standard deviation of the heartbeat intervals measured by the heart rate sensor. HRV is for users over the age of 18.

If the difference between the two heartbeat intervals is not large, the HRV is relatively low; otherwise, the HRV is relatively high. The higher the HRV, the better, representing better cardiovascular performance and stress tolerance.

Lactate Threshold Heart Rate refers to the critical heart rate corresponding to the start of a sharp rise in blood lactate concentration during exercise in the human body. It is a key physiological indicator for measuring the transition of the body from mainly aerobic metabolism to enhanced anaerobic metabolism. A higher lactate threshold heart rate indicates a stronger ability of the body to maintain aerobic metabolism during high–intensity exercise.

Lactate threshold speed refers to the critical running speed corresponding to the start of a sharp rise in blood lactate concentration during exercise in the human body. It is a core sports performance indicator for measuring the body\'s ability to maintain aerobic metabolism during high–intensity exercise. When the running speed is lower than this threshold, the body mainly relies on aerobic energy supply and is not easy to fatigue; when exceeding it, anaerobic energy supply increases, lactate accumulation accelerates, and endurance decreases.

Why is there no sleep data when wearing a watch/bracelet to bed?
1. Create a good atmosphere environment: control the light of the sleeping environment, regulate the temperature of the sleeping environment, reduce the interference of noise;
2. Establish a regular sleep schedule: fix the time of going to sleep and waking up;
3. Adjustment of lifestyle habits: Avoid eating a lot before bedtime and regular exercise can help improve sleep quality;
4. Improve sleep mindfulness: Reduce stress and anxiety by deep breathing exercises, meditation, and progressive muscle relaxation.

Sleep is structured into two periods, Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep and Non–Rapid Eye Movement (NREM) sleep, with most dreams occurring in the REM sleep stage, and NREM consisting of deep and light sleep. A complete sleep cycle usually begins with NREM stage 1, passes through NREM stage 2, NREM stage 3, and then enters the REM sleep stage, and the whole cycle lasts about 90 – 110 minutes.

By observing the changing trends of training load and physical fitness level in the past 7 days, and based on recent training data (heart rate, sports performance, recovery status, etc.), the body\'s adaptation status to training is evaluated in real–time, which is divided into 7 states: Overreaching, Detraining, Unproductive, Maintaining, Recovery, Productive and Peaking.

Training Load refers to the total amount of physiological stimulation that the human body endures during exercise. It is a comprehensive indicator of training intensity and volume in a single session or over a period of time, usually calculated by combining exercise duration, intensity (such as heart rate, pace), etc. When the load is insufficient, it is difficult to achieve training effects; when the load is too high, it may lead to fatigue accumulation or sports injuries.

Energy Source refers to the proportion of energy supply from fat and carbohydrates in the energy consumed by the body during exercise. Low–intensity exercise is mainly fueled by fat, while high–intensity exercise is mainly fueled by carbs.

Stance Time refers to the duration that body parts are in contact with the ground. A shorter stance time indicates higher running efficiency, which helps reduce impact on joints and lower the risk of injury. Stance Time is usually very short, so it is measured in milliseconds.
Stance Balance refers to the ratio of stance time between the left and right feet. An unbalanced ratio indicates excessive pressure on one side, which may cause joint injuries or muscle strength imbalance on both sides in the long term, and is prone to sprains in the short term.When the ratio is close to 100, it tilts to the right; when it is close to 0, it tilts to the left.
Vertical Oscillation refers to the height of vertical displacement of the body's center of gravity during running. It is an important indicator for measuring motor stability and movement efficiency. Excessively large vertical oscillation can lead to energy waste and impair sports performance.
Run Power refers to the power output by the body during running. This indicator is calculated by integrating factors such as strength and speed, and can reflect running intensity more accurately.

Training effect refers to post – exercise phenomena like elevated heart rate, increased lactic acid concentration, and higher energy or oxygen consumption. The longer the training duration and the greater the intensity, the more pronounced the training effect, and the longer the body requires for recovery. It is generally divided into “aerobic effect” and “anaerobic effect”, with six levels in total:
1.No Effect ：This exercise has only a minimal or no impact on the aerobic/anaerobic fitness level.
2.Recovery ：This exercise starts to activate the aerobic/anaerobic training effect, putting the body into a recovery state for aerobic/anaerobic capacity.
3.Maintenance：This exercise helps maintain the current aerobic/anaerobic fitness level.
4.Improvement：This exercise produces a certain improvement in the aerobic/anaerobic capacity.
5.Enhancement ：This exercise can significantly enhance the aerobic/anaerobic capacity.
6.Overload ：This exercise is excessive and poses potential risks. Pay attention to ensuring adequate recovery.

Short–term Load (7 days) and Long–term Load (28 days) can be used to represent the recently completed training load and the training load completed over a long period in the past, so as to obtain the body's feedback status, which is divided into three levels: High, Optimal and Low.
Short–term vs Long–term Training Load Ratio > 1.5 (High): The recent training load is too high. It is recommended to reduce the training load to avoid injury.
Short–term vs Long–term Training Load Ratio 0.8 – 1.5 (Optimal): The recent training load is appropriate, which helps the body adapt to training.
Short–term vs Long–term Training Load Ratio < 0.8 (Low): The recent training load is insufficient, making it difficult to produce positive training adaptation. It is recommended to increase the training load to achieve positive training effects.

Remaining Physical Strength refers to the percentage of current remaining physical fitness. Recovery Time is evaluated based on feedback during exercise, referring to the time required to recover from the current physical strength value to 100%, and is calculated based on data such as Heart Rate Variability (HRV), sleep quality, and historical training load.

VO2 Max refers to the maximum volume of oxygen that the human body can intake per unit time during maximum–intensity exercise. It is a core physiological indicator for measuring cardiopulmonary function, aerobic endurance, and overall exercise capacity. It reflects the efficiency of the body in delivering and utilizing oxygen to muscles. A higher value usually indicates stronger cardiopulmonary function and better aerobic exercise endurance. The ranges and corresponding statuses are as follows: 
1. Superior (≥95)
2. Excellent (75–94) 
3. Good (50–74) 
4. Fair (25–49)
5. Poor (10–24)
6. Very Poor (<10)
